title: Mirror Orchestrator: adaptive sampling and cost-fencing for safe request duplication
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a mirror traffic orchestration component that duplicates a controlled fraction of production requests to candidate model backends while enforcing per-tenant cost fences and strict isolation. The goal is to enable higher-fidelity model evaluations (full-request and response parity) without exposing production traffic to risk or unbounded spend.
background: We currently have ad-hoc shadowing pipelines used for offline evaluation and selective A/B testing. Those pipelines either duplicate too much traffic (cost overruns) or are too coarse (binary on/off), and they lack tenant-level safety gates. Previous tickets focused on sampling strategies and tenant throttles, but the platform lacks a central orchestrator that combines adaptive sampling, budget fencing, and end-to-end observability for mirrored flows.
goals: 1) Provide per-tenant and per-route cost fences for mirrored traffic. 2) Implement adaptive sampling algorithms that prioritize requests likely to produce informative deltas. 3) Ensure mirrored requests are isolated (no side-effects, no downstream external calls) and idempotent. 4) Expose metrics and alerts for mirror cost, delta rate, and model divergence. 5) Support fast rollback/cutoff if mirrored experiments breach safety thresholds.
non_goals: 1) This ticket does not implement new model comparison UIs; analytics will be emitted to existing observability pipelines. 2) Does not change the core runtime request path latency SLA for non-mirrored traffic.
proposal: Introduce a Mirror Orchestrator service sitting in the request gateway path. It will: 1) Evaluate per-request mirror eligibility using configurable filters (route, tenant, headers, size). 2) Use an adaptive sampler that increases sampling for inputs with high model-variance signals (e.g., hallucination risk markers) and decreases sampling when cost budgets are near limits. 3) Attach a per-tenant cost token and reject or throttle mirroring when risk/budget thresholds are hit. 4) Send mirrored copies to isolated mirror clusters with scrubbed telemetry and controlled side-effect suppression. 5) Record correlation IDs and response diffs to the eval pipeline for automatic regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: Mirror Orchestrator deployed behind the gateway in staging and can accept a flag to enable mirroring per-route.
Adaptive sampler supports at least two strategies: uniform probability and variance-priority (based on model difference signals).
Per-tenant cost fence enforced: when budget is exceeded, mirroring for that tenant is suspended and an event is emitted.
Mirrored requests are sent to a sandboxed endpoint that blocks external side-effects (network calls, DB writes) by default.
End-to-end tracing present: original request ID correlates to mirrored request IDs and response diffs are annotated in traces.
Automated rollback: a threshold-based cut-off policy (e.g., delta-rate > 5% or mirror-cost > 120% of budget) triggers immediate suspension and a PagerDuty alert.
Unit and integration tests covering eligibility filters, sampler behavior, cost fence paths, and isolation toggles exist and pass in CI.
implementation_steps: Design: finalize API for mirror eligibility and per-tenant budget tokens (design doc: drive/redwood/mirror-orchestrator-v1).
Infra: provision isolated mirror clusters with sandbox policies and create IAM roles (eng-ops task).
Server: implement orchestrator service with pluggable samplers and token bucket cost fences.
Runtime integration: gateway hook to call orchestrator asynchronously for eligible requests with non-blocking paths for production latency preservation.
Observability: emit metrics (mirror_count, mirror_cost, delta_rate, suspend_events) to Console and create dashboards/alerts.
Safety: implement side-effect suppression layer in mirror cluster and test deterministic idempotency for duplicated requests.
Testing: run canary in staging, then run canary in a small subset of production customers with explicit owner agreement.
Launch: gradual ramping, monitoring, and post-launch retrospective.
Cleanup: deprecate older ad-hoc mirror scripts and provide migration guide for teams.
rollout_plan: Week 1: deploy orchestrator to staging; integration tests and smoke test with synthetic traffic.
Week 2: enable for internal tenants only (dev tenants) with very low sampling (0.1%) to validate traces and diffs.
Week 3: open to opt-in partner customers at controlled sample rates and validate cost fencing behavior under load.
Week 4: ramp to broader tenant cohorts once delta-rate stability and cost metrics are acceptable.
Rollback: immediate suspension if cost fence trips or delta-rate crosses critical threshold; manual investigation and reconfiguration follow.
risks: Unintended production impact if the gateway hook becomes blocking—mitigation: async fire-and-forget with backpressure protection.
Cost spikes from poorly calibrated samplers—mitigation: start with conservative defaults and hard budget fences per tenant.
False positives in delta detection causing unnecessary suspensions—mitigation: use rolling windows and hysteresis before triggering full suspend.
Data privacy risk if mirrored payloads contain PII—mitigation: implement payload scrubbing rules and per-tenant opt-out flags.
Complexity of correlation across traces—mitigation: standardize correlation-id propagation and instrument key touchpoints.
testing_plan: Unit tests for eligibility logic and sampler correctness (deterministic RNG seeds).
Integration tests that simulate different tenant budgets and assert suspend/resume behavior.
Chaos test: simulate mirror cluster timeouts and ensure original request latency unaffected and fallback is quiet.
End-to-end test with synthetic model variants to measure delta-rate detection and evaluate alerting thresholds.
